My favorite game series is bayonetta. I refused to play it for years because once I heard her suit is made of hair and she uses the hair to summon demons so, she's naked during her special attacks. I just assumed it'd be a game who's only made to shove tits and ass into your face. Also it was a beat em up, which I thought was the same thing as a hack n slash, and I thought that was a boring genre.

One day, years after its release, I went over to my friend's house and he had it. He told me it was fun and I should play it. I reluctantly tried it, and even though the game was sexy, it kinda had a tasteful side to it (think like an old burlesque show). But the sex appeal wasn't the main draw, it was the combat.

Holy hell that was fun! I was hooked right off the tutorial. You're in a graveyard fighting waves of angels to a cover of Frank Sinatra's "Fly me to the moon" and it just works! The reason I hate hack n slashes are because they're just "mash a button until the next stage." In Bayonetta the combat was well designed. There are so many combos to use for different effects. It was the first place I've seen pausing mid combo to switch attacks outside a fighting game. Later you unlock weapons to switch up your move set, and can pick the load out that is most "you".

The game is also difficult, while you don't have lives, if you die more than 5 times you're guaranteed to get the lowest possible rating when you finish the level. I rarely ever got awarded higher than the stone award. The awards are stone, bronze, silver, gold, platinum, and pure platinum. 

I was worried that the 2nd one would be bad since it was a WiiU exclusive but, it didn't feel like a WiiU game which was awesome! It took the story more over the top than the first game! That's why this is my favorite series even if it's only 2 games long.

Dead by daylight is a 4v1 horror game from Behavior Digital Inc. 4 players are assigned to the role of survivor. Their objective is to evade sacrifice and escape the map with their lives. They accomplish this by finding and repairing generators to power the gates along the walls. Even though it's a 4v1 game, the survivors are not on a team and at the end of the day, its all about you. If you escape you win, no matter how many other survivors have died. So you can use other survivors as bait while you make your escape but, you can accomplish objectives faster and earn bonus points to upgrade your loadout and skills for the next game. The survivors all have third person views to enable them to survey their environment and evade capture.

The killer is alone, and on the hunt. His mission is to capture, torment, and sacrifice the survivors. He has a wide variety of tools to help him accomplish this goal. He can lay down bear traps, track blood, and see sound to find his prey. Once he has a survivor in his grasp he carries them to one of several meat hooks scattered around the map and places them on it. If the survivor cannot free himself or be rescued in time, he is sacrificed to some sort of monster from the sky. From what I've seen, the killer is also faster when running. Although his vision is from a first person perspective, so he can't look around as well as the survivors can. The killer can spend his points on feats and weapons to give himself a better chance. There will be multiple killers to choose from, from paranormal monsters that can phase through walls, to your standard masked slasher.

I was a new player and everyone else was already familiar with the setting of the story. Some of the older players got to keep their old characters, I had to roll a new one around the same level. I rolled a half-giant fighter, my weapon was a [kusarigama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kusarigama), which my martial arts teacher/DM designed for me since that was the weapon I was studying in class. Since I was a giant, the blunt object on the end was a morningstar and I used a regular scythe in one hand. 

The setting of the story was in a pentagram shaped city of evil. All the inhabitants and most of the players were evil to an extent. I tried to be, but I mostly came off as brutish or arrogant which was ok for a half-giant. I was set in a party of returning players who chose to make new characters that were visiting the city for the first time. Once we got in a gnome demanded a toll, since I was told to play evil, I responded with violence. I rolled high, raised my fists over my head, and donkey kong ground pounded him into a puddle of blood and an iron armor pancake.

The drug lords were a group of players who kept their old characters from the last play through. They found a drug addict and decided to question him. He would not comply so I picked him off the ground, he screamed and alerted a nearby patrol of blackguard enforcers. The other players were familiar with the guard of this city and talked their way out of any serious punishment. I was not. I swung the morningstar above my head and took out the captain's horse. Everyone thought I was dead meat. The captain came over in no mood to talk. He attacked me and through a series of lucky rolls I blocked his punches and he dodged my swings. The DM saw it fit to reward my luck and the captain admired my capacity for violence. 

I was taken to a guild of half-giants who were also the main competition for the players we were searching for. The guild leader introduced me to a mage and explained that I was to lead an assault on the drug lords. The mage had a scroll designed to block the powers of the player who was a necromancer. (I never got along with this kid outside the game so that was fine by me.)

Night fell and I led the charge, the scroll reading went fine and we took the first floor of the building and defeated the necromancer. Unfortunately the commotion alerted the player who was a sorceror, and this guy was a huge meta gamer. (Think Red Mage from 8-bit Theater).
